tools.name: exec

format.definition:
start: pragma_source | plain_source
pragma_source: PRAGMA_LINE NEWLINE SOURCE
plain_source: SOURCE

PRAGMA_LINE: /[ \t]*\/\/ @exec:[^\r\n]*/
NEWLINE: /\r?\n/
SOURCE: /[\s\S]+/

tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.name: request_user_input
tools.description: Request user input for one to three short questions and wait for the response. This tool is only available in Plan mode.

questions.description: Questions to show the user. Prefer 1 and do not exceed 3

header.description: Short header label shown in the UI (12 or fewer chars).

options.description: Provide 2-3 mutually exclusive choices. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with "(Recommended)". Do not include an "Other" option in this list; the client will add a free-form "Other" option automatically.

description.description: One short sentence explaining impact/tradeoff if selected.

question.description: Single-sentence prompt shown to the user.

tools.name: request_user_input_async
tools.description: Ask the user one or more questions during ongoing work. Use this tool only to request missing information, preferences, constraints, clarification, or approval. The tool returns immediately without ending the turn or waiting for a reply; any reply arrives asynchronously as a new user message. Keep questions concise, self-contained, and easy to understand, using a level of detail appropriate to the user and task. The UI always allows a free-text answer, including when suggested options are provided. A preselected option is not submitted automatically.

questions.description: One or more self-contained questions to present together, in display order.

options.description: Suggested answers, in display order. Put the recommended answer first; the first option is preselected by default. The user can select one option or enter a free-text answer. Do not include an Other option or a free-text placeholder; the UI provides free-text input automatically. Omit options for a free-text-only question.

title.description: The complete question shown to the user, including any context needed to answer it.

tools.name: send_message_to_user_async
tools.description: Send a concise message that needs the user's attention during ongoing work. The tool returns immediately without ending the turn or waiting for a reply; any reply arrives asynchronously as a new user message. Use this tool to report a critical blocker or a finding that may change the task's direction, or to answer a user question or status request received while work is still in progress. Use this tool when a message needs the user's immediate attention; use commentary for routine progress and intermediate context. Use clear formatting, such as bolding questions, to make requests easy to notice and answer.

message.description: The concise question or update to send to the user.

tools.name: clock
tools.description: Tools for reading and waiting on time.

tools.name: sleep
tools.description: Pause execution for a specified duration. The sleep ends early when new input arrives for the active turn. Returns the elapsed wall-clock time.

duration_ms.description: How long to sleep in milliseconds. Must be between 1 and 43200000.

tools.name: collaboration
tools.description: Tools for spawning and managing sub-agents.

tools.name: followup_task
tools.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing non-root target agent and trigger a turn if it is idle. If the target is already running, deliver the task promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes.

message.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to send a follow-up task to (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List live agents in the current root thread tree. Optionally filter by task-path prefix.

path_prefix.description: Task-path prefix filter without a trailing slash. Omit to list all live agents.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `gpt-6.2-sol`: Fast, go-to model for coding and everyday work. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6.2-astra`: Our most capable model for complex coding and professional work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6.1-sol`: Previous generation model for coding and everyday work. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6.1-terra`: Efficient model that excels at visual understanding and computer use. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-astra`: Previous generation model for complex coding and professional work. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

fork_turns.description: Parent history to inherit. Defaults to `all`; use `none` to start without parent history. Only `all` and `none` are supported.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

<permissions instructions>
Filesystem sandboxing defines which files can be read or written. `sandbox_mode` is `workspace-write`: The sandbox permits reading files, and editing files in `cwd` and `writable_roots`. Editing files in other directories requires approval. Network access is restricted.
# Escalation Requests

Commands are run outside the sandbox if they are approved by the user, or match an existing rule that allows it to run unrestricted. The command string is split into independent command segments at shell control operators, including but not limited to:

- Pipes: |
- Logical operators: &&, ||
- Command separators: ;
- Subshell boundaries: (...), $(...)

Each resulting segment is evaluated independently for sandbox restrictions and approval requirements.

Example:

git pull | tee output.txt

This is treated as two command segments:

["git", "pull"]

["tee", "output.txt"]

Commands that use more advanced shell features like redirection (>, >>, <), substitutions ($(...), ...), environment variables (FOO=bar), or wildcard patterns (*, ?) will not be evaluated against rules, to limit the scope of what an approved rule allows.

## How to request escalation

IMPORTANT: To request approval to execute a command that will require escalated privileges:

- Provide the `sandbox_permissions` parameter with the value `"require_escalated"`
- Include a short question asking the user if they want to allow the action in `justification` parameter. e.g. "Do you want to download and install dependencies for this project?"
- Optionally suggest a `prefix_rule` - this will be shown to the user with an option to persist the rule approval for future sessions.

If you run a command that is important to solving the user's query, but it fails because of sandboxing or with a likely sandbox-related network error (for example DNS/host resolution, registry/index access, or dependency download failure), rerun the command with "require_escalated". ALWAYS proceed to use the `justification` parameter - do not message the user before requesting approval for the command.

## When to request escalation

While commands are running inside the sandbox, here are some scenarios that will require escalation outside the sandbox:

- You need to run a command that writes to a directory that requires it (e.g. running tests that write to /var)
- You need to run a GUI app (e.g., open/xdg-open/osascript) to open browsers or files.
- If you run a command that is important to solving the user's query, but it fails because of sandboxing or with a likely sandbox-related network error (for example DNS/host resolution, registry/index access, or dependency download failure), rerun the command with `require_escalated`. ALWAYS proceed to use the `sandbox_permissions` and `justification` parameters. do not message the user before requesting approval for the command.
- You are about to take a potentially destructive action such as an `rm` or `git reset` that the user did not explicitly ask for.
- Be judicious with escalating, but if completing the user's request requires it, you should do so - don't try and circumvent approvals by using other tools.

## prefix_rule guidance

When choosing a `prefix_rule`, request one that will allow you to fulfill similar requests from the user in the future without re-requesting escalation. It should be categorical and reasonably scoped to similar capabilities. You should rarely pass the entire command into `prefix_rule`.

### Banned prefix_rules 
Avoid requesting overly broad prefixes that the user would be ill-advised to approve. For example, do not request ["python3"], ["python", "-"], or other similar prefixes that would allow arbitrary scripting.
NEVER provide a prefix_rule argument for destructive commands like rm.
NEVER provide a prefix_rule if your command uses a heredoc or herestring. 

### Examples
Good examples of prefixes:
- ["npm", "run", "dev"]
- ["gh", "pr", "check"]
- ["cargo", "test"]


## Approved command prefixes
The following prefix rules have already been approved: - ["git", "add"]
- ["uv", "lock"]
- ["uv", "sync"]
- ["git", "commit"]
- ["git", "diff", "--cached", "--check"]
 The writable roots are `/home/user/ai-full-stack-it-access-requests`, `/tmp`.

<multi_agent_role>You are `/root`, the primary agent in a team of agents collaborating to fulfill the user's goals.

At the start of your turn, you are the active agent. Your final answer will be the response to the user
All agents in the team have access to the same set of tools.

All agents share the same workspace, filesystem, and tool state, meaning any changes will be immediately reflected in your local state.

With `fork_turns="all"` (the default), the child can see the parent’s conversation up to the fork. With `"none"`, it starts without that conversation. In either case, the child receives its own role and task.

You will receive messages in the commentary channel in the form:
```
Message Type: MESSAGE | FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: <recipient>
Sender: <author>
Payload:
<payload text>
```
They will be preceded by a header of the form `assistant:<sender> to=/root`
Note that collaboration tools cannot be called from inside `functions.exec`. Call `spawn_agent`, `send_message`, `followup_task`, `wait_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, and `list_agents` only as direct tool calls using the recipient shown in their tool definitions, such as `to=functions.collaboration.spawn_agent`, since they are intentionally absent from the `functions.exec` `tools.*` namespace. Available tools in `functions.exec` are explicitly described with a `tools` namespace in the developer message.

All agents share the same directory. In detail:
- All agents have access to the same container and filesystem as you.
- All agents use the same current working directory.
- As a result, edits made by one agent are immediately visible to all other agents.

When calling `wait_agent`, prefer longer waits (minutes) to avoid busy polling.

There are 4 available concurrency slots, meaning that up to 4 agents can be active at once, including you.

Full-history forks (`fork_turns` omitted or `"all"`) inherit the parent model and reasoning effort and do not accept overrides. Only set `model` or `reasoning_effort` when explicitly requested by the user, applicable `AGENTS.md` instructions, or skill instructions; when doing so, set `fork_turns` to `"none"`.</multi_agent_role>

Submit only the root repository link (`https://github.com//`) through the Classroom assignment.” # Build plan for the IT access-request intake This plan implements `planning/spec.md` R-01–R-105 using the four source documents and all 20 request messages. Only this plan is being written now. All module paths, commands, tests, fixtures and outputs below are proposed future work; none is reported as implemented, run or passing. Implementation choices below are choices for satisfying the spec, not new source requirements. No application code, tests, fixtures, dependency changes, outputs, commits or submissions belong to this planning task. ## Choices - **Runtime:** Python 3.11 or later, standard-library `unittest`, `sqlite3`, `argparse`, hashing and HTTP transport, with `jsonschema` declared in `pyproject.toml` and dependencies locked in `uv.lock`; this fits the supplied Python test harness and keeps deployment small. - **Interface:** a CLI invoked as `python3 -m intake`, with `run`, `queue`, `resume`, `retry`, `history`, `export` and `accuracy` subcommands; separate invocations can inspect committed results while intake continues, and the same commands support handover and recovery. - **Tests:** `env -u API_KEY python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`, plus the spec’s individual `-k test_rNN_contract` filters; tests use temporary directories/databases, deterministic scripted responses and a blocked real network, so no test or build step needs a real API_KEY. - **Model provider:** a provider interface with a scripted mock and a configurable OpenAI Responses adapter over an injected HTTPS JSON transport; request model ID, endpoint, request settings and timeout are explicit configuration, with production authentication read only from API_KEY and no credential stored in configuration fingerprints. Verify the exact supported request/response fields against current official provider documentation before implementation, record the chosen model ID/configuration in README and evidence, and test the real adapter entirely through intercepted transport rather than a live call. The initial supported shared-operation arrangement is multiple CLI processes on one host using one local SQLite database; filesystem/network-share and multi-host database behavior are outside this arrangement and will be documented rather than claimed as tested. L229: #### E205.4 Accessibility Standard
L230: 
L233: ##### E205.4.1 Word Substitution when Applying WCAG to Non-Web Documents
L234: 
L235: For non-Web documents, wherever the term “Web page” or “page” appears in WCAG 2.0 Level A and AA Success Criteria and Conformance Requirements, the term “document” shall be substituted for the terms “Web page” and “page”. In addition, in Success Criterion in 1.4.2, the phrase “in a document” shall be substituted for the phrase “on a Web page”.
L236: 
L237: ### E206 Hardware
L238: #### E206.1 General
L239: 
L240: Where components of ICT are hardware and transmit information or have a user interface, such components shall conform to the requirements in Chapter 4.
L241: 
L242: ### E207 Software
L243: #### E207.1 General
L244: 
L245: Where components of ICT are software and transmit information or have a user interface, such components shall conform to E207 and the requirements in Chapter 5.
L246: EXCEPTION: Software that is assistive technology and that supports the accessibility services of the platform shall not be required to conform to the requirements in Chapter 5.
L247: #### E207.2 WCAG Conformance
L248: 
L249: User interface components, as well as the content of platforms and applications, shall conform to Level A and Level AA Success Criteria and Conformance Requirements in WCAG 2.0 (incorporated by reference, see 702.10.1).
L250: EXCEPTIONS:
L251:   1. Software that is assistive technology and that supports the accessibility services of the platform shall not be required to conform to E207.2.
L252:   2. Non-Web software shall not be required to conform to the following four Success Criteria in WCAG 2.0: 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks; 2.4.5 Multiple Ways; 3.2.3 Consistent Navigation; and 3.2.4 Consistent Identification.
L253:   3. Non-Web software shall not be required to conform to Conformance Requirement 3 Complete Processes in WCAG 2.0.
L254: ##### E207.2.1 Word Substitution when Applying WCAG to Non-Web Software
L255: 
L256: For non-Web software, wherever the term “Web page” or “page” appears in WCAG 2.0 Level A and AA Success Criteria and Conformance Requirements, the term “software” shall be substituted for the terms “Web page” and “page”. In addition, in Success Criterion in 1.4.2, the phrase “in software” shall be substituted for the phrase “on a Web page.”
L257: #### E207.3 Complete Processes for Non-Web Software
L258: 
L259: Where non-Web software requires multiple steps to accomplish an activity, all software related to the activity to be accomplished shall conform to WCAG 2.0 as specified in E207.2.
L260: 
L261: ### E208 Support Documentation and Services
L262: 
L263: #### E208.1 General
L264: 
L265: Where an agency provides support documentation or services for ICT, such documentation and services shall conform to the requirements in Chapter 6.
L266: 
L267: * * *
L268: # Appendix B to Part 1194 – Section 255 of the Communications Act: Application and Scoping Requirements
L269: 
L270: ## 255 Chapter 1: Application and Administration
L271: 
L272: ### C101 General
L273: #### C101.1 Purpose
L274: These Revised 255 Guidelines, which consist of 255 Chapters 1 and 2 (Appendix B), along with Chapters 3 through 7 (Appendix C), contain scoping and technical requirements for the design, development, and fabrication of telecommunications equipment and customer premises equipment, content, and support documentation and services, to ensure accessibility and usability by individuals with disabilities.
L275: These Revised 255 Guidelines are to be applied to the extent required by regulations issued by the Federal Communications Commission under Section 255 of the Communications Act of 1934, as amended (47 U.S.C. 255).
L276: #### C101.2 Equivalent Facilitation
L277: The use of an alternative design or technology that results in substantially equivalent or greater accessibility and usability by individuals with disabilities than would be provided by conformance to one or more of the requirements in Chapters 4 and 5 of the Revised 255 Guidelines is permitted. The functional performance criteria in Chapter 3 shall be used to determine whether substantially equivalent or greater accessibility and usability is provided to individuals with disabilities.
L278: #### C101.3 Conventional Industry Tolerances
L279: 
L280: Dimensions are subject to conventional industry tolerances except where dimensions are stated as a range with specific minimum or maximum end points.
L281: 
L282: #### C101.4 Units of Measurement
L283: 
L284: Measurements are stated in metric and U.S. customary units. The values stated in each system (metric and U.S. customary units) may not be exact equivalents, and each system shall be used independently of the other.
L285: 
L286: ### C102 Referenced Standards
L287: #### C102.1 Application
L288: 
L289: The specific editions of the standards listed in Chapter 7 are incorporated by reference into 255 Chapter 2 (Scoping Requirements) and Chapters 3 through 6 to the prescribed extent of each such reference. Where conflicts occur between the Revised 255 Guidelines and the referenced standards, these Revised 255 Guidelines apply.

L185: ##### E202.7.2 Alternative Means
L186: 
L187: Where ICT that fully conforms to the Revised 508 Standards is not commercially available, the agency shall provide individuals with disabilities access to and use of information and data by an alternative means that meets identified needs.
L188: 
L189: ### E203 Access to Functionality
L190: #### E203.1 General
L191: 
L192: Agencies shall ensure that all functionality of ICT is accessible to and usable by individuals with disabilities, either directly or by supporting the use of assistive technology, and shall comply with E203. In providing access to all functionality of ICT, agencies shall ensure the following:
L193:   1. That Federal employees with disabilities have access to and use of information and data that is comparable to the access and use by Federal employees who are not individuals with disabilities; and
L194:   2. That members of the public with disabilities who are seeking information or data from a Federal agency have access to and use of information and data that is comparable to that provided to members of the public who are not individuals with disabilities.
L195: #### E203.2 User Needs
L196: 
L197: When agencies procure, develop, maintain or use ICT they shall identify the needs of users with disabilities to determine:
L198: 
L199:   1. How users with disabilities will perform the functions supported by the ICT; and
L200:   2. How the ICT will be developed, installed, configured, and maintained to support users with disabilities.
L201: 
L202: ### E204 Functional Performance Criteria
L203: #### E204.1 General
L204: 
L205: Where the requirements in Chapters 4 and 5 do not address one or more functions of ICT, the functions not addressed shall conform to the Functional Performance Criteria specified in Chapter 3.
L206: 
L207: ### E205 Electronic Content
L208: 
L209: #### E205.1 General
L210: 
L211: Electronic content shall comply with E205.
L212: 
L213: #### E205.2 Public Facing
L214: 
L215: Electronic content that is public facing shall conform to the accessibility requirements specified in E205.4.
L216: #### E205.3 Agency Official Communication
L217: 
L218: Electronic content that is not public facing shall conform to the accessibility requirements specified in E205.4 when such content constitutes official business and is communicated by an agency through one or more of the following:
L219:   1. An emergency notification;
L220:   2. An initial or final decision adjudicating an administrative claim or proceeding;
L221:   3. An internal or external program or policy announcement;
L222:   4. A notice of benefits, program eligibility, employment opportunity, or personnel action;
L223:   5. A formal acknowledgement of receipt;
L224:   6. A survey questionnaire;
L225:   7. A template or form;
L226:   8. Educational or training materials; or
L227:   9. Intranet content designed as a Web page.
L228: EXCEPTION: Records maintained by the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) pursuant to Federal recordkeeping statutes shall not be required to conform to the Revised 508 Standards unless public facing.
L229: #### E205.4 Accessibility Standard
L230: 
L231: Electronic content shall conform to Level A and Level AA Success Criteria and Conformance Requirements in WCAG 2.0 (incorporated by reference, see 702.10.1).
L232: EXCEPTION: Non-Web documents shall not be required to conform to the following four WCAG 2.0 Success Criteria: 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks, 2.4.5 Multiple Ways, 3.2.3 Consistent Navigation, and 3.2.4 Consistent Identification.

L234:

In addition, in Success Criterion in 1.4.2, the phrase “in a document” shall be substituted for the phrase “on a Web page”.

L238: #### E206.1 General
L239: 
L240: Where components of ICT are hardware and transmit information or have a user interface, such components shall conform to the requirements in Chapter 4.
L241: 
L242: ### E207 Software
L243: #### E207.1 General
L244: 
L245: Where components of ICT are software and transmit information or have a user interface, such components shall conform to E207 and the requirements in Chapter 5.
L246: EXCEPTION: Software that is assistive technology and that supports the accessibility services of the platform shall not be required to conform to the requirements in Chapter 5.
L247: #### E207.2 WCAG Conformance
L248: 
L249: User interface components, as well as the content of platforms and applications, shall conform to Level A and Level AA Success Criteria and Conformance Requirements in WCAG 2.0 (incorporated by reference, see 702.10.1).
L250: EXCEPTIONS:
L251:   1. Software that is assistive technology and that supports the accessibility services of the platform shall not be required to conform to E207.2.

L767: ##### 413.1.1 Decoding and Display of Closed Captions
L768: 
L769: Players and displays shall decode closed caption data and support display of captions.
L770: 
L771: ##### 413.1.2 Pass-Through of Closed Caption Data
L772: 
L773: Cabling and ancillary equipment shall pass through caption data.
L774: 
L775: ### 414 Audio Description Processing Technologies
L776: 
L777: #### 414.1 General
L778: 
L779: Where ICT displays or processes video with synchronized audio, ICT shall provide audio description processing technology conforming to 414.1.1 or 414.1.2.
L780: ##### 414.1.1 Digital Television Tuners
L781: 
L782: Digital television tuners shall provide audio description processing that conforms to ATSC A/53 Digital Television Standard, Part 5 (2014) (incorporated by reference, see 702.2.1). Digital television tuners shall provide processing of audio description when encoded as a Visually Impaired (VI) associated audio service that is provided as a complete program mix containing audio description according to the ATSC A/53 standard.
L783: ##### 414.1.2 Other ICT
L784: 
L785: ICT other than digital television tuners shall provide audio description processing.
L786: 
L787: ### 415 User Controls for Captions and Audio Descriptions
L788: #### 415.1 General
L789: 
L790: Where ICT displays video with synchronized audio, ICT shall provide user controls for closed captions and audio descriptions conforming to 415.1.
L791: EXCEPTION: Devices for personal use shall not be required to conform to 415.1 provided that captions and audio descriptions can be enabled through system-wide platform settings.
L792: 
L793: ##### 415.1.1 Caption Controls
L794: 
L795: Where ICT provides operable parts for volume control, ICT shall also provide operable parts for caption selection.
L796: ##### 415.1.2 Audio Description Controls
L797: 
L798: Where ICT provides operable parts for program selection, ICT shall also provide operable parts for the selection of audio description.
L799: 
L800: * * *
L801: 
L802: ## Chapter 5: Software
L803: 
L804: ### 501 General
L805: #### 501.1 Scope
L806: The requirements of Chapter 5 shall apply to software where required by 508 Chapter 2 (Scoping Requirements), 255 Chapter 2 (Scoping Requirements), and where otherwise referenced in any other chapter of the Revised 508 Standards or Revised 255 Guidelines.
L807: EXCEPTION: Where Web applications do not have access to platform accessibility services and do not include components that have access to platform accessibility services, they shall not be required to conform to 502 or 503 provided that they conform to Level A and Level AA Success Criteria and Conformance Requirements in WCAG 2.0 (incorporated by reference, see 702.10.1).
L808: ### 502 Interoperability with Assistive Technology
L809: 
L810: #### 502.1 General
L811: 
L812: Software shall interoperate with assistive technology and shall conform to 502.
L813: EXCEPTION: ICT conforming to 402 shall not be required to conform to 502.
L814: 
L815: #### 502.2 Documented Accessibility Features
L816: 
L817: Software with platform features defined in platform documentation as accessibility features shall conform to 502.2.
L818: ##### 502.2.1 User Control of Accessibility Features
L819: 
L820: Platform software shall provide user control over platform features that are defined in the platform documentation as accessibility features.
L821: 
L822: ##### 502.2.2 No Disruption of Accessibility Features
L823: 
L824: Software shall not disrupt platform features that are defined in the platform documentation as accessibility features.
L825: #### 502.3 Accessibility Services
L826: 
L827: Platform software and software tools that are provided by the platform developer shall provide a documented set of accessibility services that support applications running on the platform to interoperate with assistive technology and shall conform to 502.3. Applications that are also platforms shall expose the underlying platform accessibility services or implement other documented accessibility services.
L828: ##### 502.3.1 Object Information
L829: 
L830: The object role, state(s), properties, boundary, name, and description shall be programmatically determinable.
L831: 
L832: ##### 502.3.2 Modification of Object Information
L833: 
L834: States and properties that can be set by the user shall be capable of being set programmatically, including through assistive technology.
L835: ##### 502.3.3 Row, Column, and Headers
L836: 
L837: If an object is in a data table, the occupied rows and columns, and any headers associated with those rows or columns, shall be programmatically determinable.
L838: 
L839: ##### 502.3.4 Values
L840: 
L841: Any current value(s), and any set or range of allowable values associated with an object, shall be programmatically determinable.
L842: ##### 502.3.5 Modification of Values
L843: 
L844: Values that can be set by the user shall be capable of being set programmatically, including through assistive technology.
L845: 
L846: ##### 502.3.6 Label Relationships
L847: 
L848: Any relationship that a component has as a label for another component, or of being labeled by another component, shall be programmatically determinable.
L849: ##### 502.3.7 Hierarchical Relationships
L850: 
L851: Any hierarchical (parent-child) relationship that a component has as a container for, or being contained by, another component shall be programmatically determinable.
L852: 
L853: ##### 502.3.8 Text
L854: 
L855: The content of text objects, text attributes, and the boundary of text rendered to the screen, shall be programmatically determinable.
L856: ##### 502.3.9 Modification of Text
L857: 
L858: Text that can be set by the user shall be capable of being set programmatically, including through assistive technology.
L859: 
L860: ##### 502.3.10 List of Actions
L861: 
L862: A list of all actions that can be executed on an object shall be programmatically determinable.
L863: 
L864: ##### 502.3.11 Actions on Objects
L865: 
L866: Applications shall allow assistive technology to programmatically execute available actions on objects.

L925: #### 504.3 Prompts
L926: 
L927: Authoring tools shall provide a mode of operation that prompts authors to create content that conforms to Level A and Level AA Success Criteria and Conformance Requirements in WCAG 2.0 (incorporated by reference, see 702.10.1) for supported features and, as applicable, to file formats supported by the authoring tool.

L15: 29 U.S.C. 794d: Electronic and information technology Text contains those laws in effect through Public Law 119-136 (October 22, 2026).
L16: 
L17: From Title 29-LABOR CHAPTER 16-VOCATIONAL REHABILITATION AND OTHER REHABILITATION SERVICES
L18: 
L20: ### §794d. Electronic and information technology
L21: 
L22: (a)  Requirements for Federal departments and agencies
L23: 
L24: (1)  Accessibility
L25: 
L26: (A)  Development, procurement, maintenance, or use of electronic and information technology
L27: When developing, procuring, maintaining, or using electronic and information technology, each Federal department or agency, including the United States Postal Service, shall ensure, unless an undue burden would be imposed on the department or agency, that the electronic and information technology allows, regardless of the type of medium of the technology⁠—
L28: (i)  individuals with disabilities who are Federal employees to have access to and use of information and data that is comparable to the access to and use of the information and data by Federal employees who are not individuals with disabilities; and
L29: (ii)  individuals with disabilities who are members of the public seeking information or services from a Federal department or agency to have access to and use of information and data that is comparable to the access to and use of the information and data by such members of the public who are not individuals with disabilities.
L30: 
L31: (B)  Alternative means efforts
L32: When development, procurement, maintenance, or use of electronic and information technology that meets the standards published by the Access Board under paragraph (2) would impose an undue burden, the Federal department or agency shall provide individuals with disabilities covered by paragraph (1) with the information and data involved by an alternative means of access that allows the individual to use the information and data.
L33: 
L34: (2)  Electronic and information technology standards
L35: 
L36: (A)  In general
L37: Not later than 18 months after August 7, 1998, the Architectural and Transportation Barriers Compliance Board (referred to in this section as the “Access Board”), after consultation with the Secretary of Education, the Administrator of General Services, the Secretary of Commerce, the Chairman of the Federal Communications Commission, the Secretary of Defense, and the head of any other Federal department or agency that the Access Board determines to be appropriate, including consultation on relevant research findings, and after consultation with the electronic and information technology industry and appropriate public or nonprofit agencies or organizations, including organizations representing individuals with disabilities, shall issue and publish standards setting forth⁠—
L38: (i)  for purposes of this section, a definition of electronic and information technology that is consistent with the definition of information technology specified in section 11101(6) of title 40; and
L39: 
L40: (ii)  the technical and functional performance criteria necessary to implement the requirements set forth in paragraph (1).
L41: 
L42: (B)  Review and amendment
L43: The Access Board shall periodically review and, as appropriate, amend the standards required under subparagraph (A) to reflect technological advances or changes in electronic and information technology.
L44: 
L45: (3)  Incorporation of standards
L46: Not later than 6 months after the Access Board publishes the standards required under paragraph (2), the Federal Acquisition Regulatory Council shall revise the Federal Acquisition Regulation and each Federal department or agency shall revise the Federal procurement policies and directives under the control of the department or agency to incorporate those standards.
L47: Not later than 6 months after the Access Board revises any standards required under paragraph (2), the Council shall revise the Federal Acquisition Regulation and each appropriate Federal department or agency shall revise the procurement policies and directives, as necessary, to incorporate the revisions.
L48: (4)  Acquisition planning
L49: 
L50: In the event that a Federal department or agency determines that compliance with the standards issued by the Access Board under paragraph (2) relating to procurement imposes an undue burden, the documentation by the department or agency supporting the procurement shall explain why compliance creates an undue burden.
L51: 
L52: (5)  Exemption for national security systems
L53: 
L54: This section shall not apply to national security systems, as that term is defined in section 11103(a) of title 40.
L55: (6)  Construction
L56: 
L57: (A)  Equipment
L58: 
L59: In a case in which the Federal Government provides access to the public to information or data through electronic and information technology, nothing in this section shall be construed to require a Federal department or agency⁠—
L60: (i)  to make equipment owned by the Federal Government available for access and use by individuals with disabilities covered by paragraph (1) at a location other than that where the electronic and information technology is provided to the public; or
L61: 
L62: (ii)  to purchase equipment for access and use by individuals with disabilities covered by paragraph (1) at a location other than that where the electronic and information technology is provided to the public.
L63: 
L64: (B)  Software and peripheral devices
L65: Except as required to comply with standards issued by the Access Board under paragraph (2), nothing in paragraph (1) requires the installation of specific accessibility-related software or the attachment of a specific accessibility-related peripheral device at a workstation of a Federal employee who is not an individual with a disability.
L66: 
L67: (b)  Technical assistance
L68: The Administrator of General Services and the Access Board shall provide technical assistance to individuals and Federal departments and agencies concerning the requirements of this section.
L69: 
L70: (c)  Agency evaluations
L71: Not later than 6 months after August 7, 1998, the head of each Federal department or agency shall evaluate the extent to which the electronic and information technology of the department or agency is accessible to and usable by individuals with disabilities described in subsection (a)(1), compared to the access to and use of the technology by individuals described in such subsection who are not individuals with disabilities, and submit a report containing the evaluation to the Attorney General.
L72: (d)  Reports
L73: 
L74: (1)  Interim report
L75: 
L76: Not later than 18 months after August 7, 1998, the Attorney General shall prepare and submit to the President a report containing information on and recommendations regarding the extent to which the electronic and information technology of the Federal Government is accessible to and usable by individuals with disabilities described in subsection (a)(1).
L77: 
L78: (2)  Biennial reports
L79: Not later than 3 years after August 7, 1998, and every 2 years thereafter, the Attorney General shall prepare and submit to the President and Congress a report containing information on and recommendations regarding the state of Federal department and agency compliance with the requirements of this section, including actions regarding individual complaints under subsection (f).
L80: 
L81: (e)  Cooperation
L82: Each head of a Federal department or agency (including the Access Board, the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, and the General Services Administration) shall provide to the Attorney General such information as the Attorney General determines is necessary to conduct the evaluations under subsection (c) and prepare the reports under subsection (d).
L83: 
L84: (f)  Enforcement
L85: 
L86: (1)  General
L87: 
L88: (A)  Complaints
L89: Effective 6 months after the date of publication by the Access Board of final standards described in subsection (a)(2), any individual with a disability may file a complaint alleging that a Federal department or agency fails to comply with subsection (a)(1) in providing electronic and information technology.
L90: 
L91: (B)  Application
L92: This subsection shall apply only to electronic and information technology that is procured by a Federal department or agency not less than 6 months after the date of publication by the Access Board of final standards described in subsection (a)(2).
L93: 
L94: (2)  Administrative complaints
L95: Complaints filed under paragraph (1) shall be filed with the Federal department or agency alleged to be in noncompliance. The Federal department or agency receiving the complaint shall apply the complaint procedures established to implement section 794 of this title for resolving allegations of discrimination in a federally conducted program or activity.
L96: 
L97: (3)  Civil actions
L98: The remedies, procedures, and rights set forth in sections 794a(a)(2) and 794a(b) of this title shall be the remedies, procedures, and rights available to any individual with a disability filing a complaint under paragraph (1).
L99: 
L100: (g)  Application to other Federal laws
L101: This section shall not be construed to limit any right, remedy, or procedure otherwise available under any provision of Federal law (including sections 791 through 794a of this title) that provides greater or equal protection for the rights of individuals with disabilities than this section.

L7: [Button: Menu]
L8: 
L9: # ICT Testing Baseline Portfolio
L10: ## Overview
L11: 
L12: The 【2†Information and Communication Technology†www.access-board.gov】 (ICT) Testing Baseline Portfolio establishes the minimum requirements for evaluating the conformance of ICT with the 【3†Revised Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973†www.access-board.gov】, as amended (29 U.S.C. 794d). These Baselines are a benchmark for test processes that determine Section 508 conformance for ICT across federal agencies.
L13: The purpose of the ICT Testing Baselines is to provide a standardized set of components for evaluating Section 508 conformance. Incorporating the Baseline tests into a test process ensures that necessary elements are tested, reducing the risk of overlooking important requirements. The Baseline provides clear guidance on what needs to be tested, helping organizations assess the accuracy of their testing methodology and tools.
L14: 
L15: What the ICT Testing Baseline Is:
L16:   * A comprehensive set of test components that a Section 508 conformance test process should include to ensure full coverage of all requirements.
L17:   * Independent of any testing tools.
L18: 
L19: What the ICT Testing Baseline Is NOT:
L20: 
L21:   * A step-by-step testing procedure or methodology.
L22:   * A specific testing tool or software for Section 508 conformance testing.
L23: The Portfolio includes a Baseline for Web and a Baseline for Documents. Additional Baselines will be developed for all ICT covered by Section 508 including software and hardware.
L24: ### Baseline for Web Accessibility
L25: 
L26: The 【4†Baseline for Web】, version 3.1 (published April 1, 2024), sets the standard for testing web content for conformance with Section 508 compliance requirements. This was the first baseline in the Portfolio and is recognized as a Best Practice by the Federal CIO Council’s Accessibility Community of Practice (ACOP). Federal agencies are encouraged to adopt this baseline when evaluating web content for accessibility.
L27: ### Baseline for Electronic Documents
L28: 
L29: The newest addition to the Portfolio, 【5†Baseline for Electronic Documents】 Version 1.0 (published September 30, 2024), sets the standard for testing all types of electronic documents for conformance with Section 508 compliance requirements. Federal agencies are encouraged to adopt this baseline when evaluating non-web electronic documents for accessibility.
L30: ### Understanding WCAG Version
L31: 
L32: While Section 508 requires WCAG 2.0 Level A and AA, Baseline tests with applicable WCAG success criteria (SC) reference the latest version (2.2) of WCAG Understanding SC articles. These updated Understanding SC articles provided improved clarity and explanations and informed the development of the Baseline tests. However, the Baselines are mapped only to Section 508 (and WCAG 2.0) requirements.
L33: ## How to Contribute
L34: 
L35: We invite you to contribute to the ongoing development of the ICT Testing Baselines. You can:
L36: 
L37:   * Fork the repository and propose improvements via issues and pull requests.
L38:   * Submit test cases to help validate test processes and tools.
L39: 
L40: The ICT Testing Baseline Working Group (ITBWG) maintains the ICT Testing Baseline Portfolio on 【6†this GitHub repository†github.com】.
L41: 
L42: Last updated: September 30, 2024

Evaluate operator-facing views of machine-readable deliverables under the software requirements. The planned CLI is non-Web software. Evaluate a service through any operator-facing client or workflow it supplies, and apply web-specific checks when a web interface is delivered. ---
name: plan-from-spec
description: Turns planning/spec.md into planning/plan.md before any code is written - ordered build steps, each naming the spec lines it meets and the test written first, with the test plan inside the plan. Use when asked to plan the build from the spec, or to write or fix the test plan.
---

# Plan from the spec

Write `planning/plan.md` from `planning/spec.md`. Write no application code and no tests in this
step: the plan is read and corrected by a person before anything is built.

## Read first

- `planning/spec.md`: the numbered requirements (R-01, R-02, ...) and how each is checked.
- `CHALLENGE.md`, `docs/requirements.md`, `materials/office-policy.md` and `snapshot.schema.json`:
  the sources the spec was written from.
- The request exports in `materials/requests/`: open the ones a test case uses, and read their
  `message` text.

## Write `planning/plan.md` with these four sections

1. **Choices.** The runtime, the interface (a CLI, a service or a web application), the test
   command, and how the model provider is called. One line each, with its reason.
2. **Steps, in build order.** A numbered list. Each step names the spec lines it meets
   (`R-03, R-07`), the test from the test plan that is written first and seen to fail, and what is
   true when the step is done. The first step builds the mock provider the tests use. Each test
   belongs to one step only, so every step has a test that fails until that step's code exists.
3. **Test plan.** A table, one row per case:

   | Case | Input | Mock response | Expected facts | Source of the expected facts | Spec lines |
   |---|---|---|---|---|---|

   - One row for each case in `docs/requirements.md` § Verification: a complete request, missing
     dates, conflicting details, embedded instructions, provider failure, an unchanged rerun and
     changed source content; then the paraphrased synthetic request, a refusal or interrupted
     response, and a failed retry after a prior success.
   - **Input** names the export file (or the new message you author) that shows the case. Find it by
     reading the messages.
   - **Mock response** says what the mock provider returns for that case: a reply saved under
     `tests/mock_responses/`, an error, or a cut-off reply. No test calls the real provider.
   - **Expected facts** are the field values, status, owner and next action the case must produce.
     Write them from the message text and the office policy, never from running the code.
   - **Source of the expected facts** quotes the words of the message and the policy rule they
     come from.
4. **Coverage.** Every spec line, each with the step that builds it and the test or check that
   shows it. A spec line with no step or no test is listed under "Not yet covered", with the reason.

## Before you finish

- Every spec line appears in § Coverage with a step and a test, or under "Not yet covered".
- Every expected fact has a quote from a message or the policy beside it.
- Every case of § Verification has its own row.
- No step and no test needs `API_KEY`.
- No test is named by two steps.

Where a spec line is unclear, say so in the plan and ask the person; do not guess a rule.
Entire's CLI is the source of truth for its own usage. Do not guess flags or
subcommands — read them from this command. You are already inside the repo:
entire auto-detects it from the git origin remote, so never ask the user for the
repo name. Pass --repo only to target a DIFFERENT repo.
Trails are project-scoped. Trail listing requires an explicit --project (--repo only filters within it), or --mine for your trails across projects.

Current repo: gh/MyWorkTraining/ai-full-stack-it-access-requests  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

When to use entire — the commands that bear on the work:
  checkpoint  Inspect and search checkpoints
                read-only except: delete, explain, push
  search      Search checkpoints, commits, and sessions using semantic and keyword matching
                read-only
  session     Manage agent sessions tracked by Entire
                read-only except: adopt, attach, resume, stop

# AI Full Stack Challenge — IT Access Requests

## The task
Northstar Labs receives access requests as free-text messages. Build a small runnable application that uses a language model to turn those messages into structured records and a review queue for the IT team. The supplied company, people and requests are fictional.

Read docs/requirements.md for the operating context and required behavior, materials/office-policy.md for review rules, and snapshot.schema.json for the record format. The 20 JSON exports in materials/requests/ are your starting data. Choose an interface suited to the IT team: a CLI, service or web application. Operators should be able to start intake, inspect completed results while other requests are pending, and resume unfinished work through the documented interface.

## What to submit
This brief ships as CHALLENGE.md; the README.md below is yours to write.

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| README.md | Setup, supported runtime/provider, exact intake/test/accuracy-check commands, environment-variable names, and how to inspect the queue |
| Source code and dependency lockfile | Runnable application, extraction prompt, schema and model request configuration |
| deliverables/extractions.jsonl | One current record per message: document_id, source_sha256, extraction (schema-conforming object, or null on error), status, owner, next_action, error (null on success), and response_source (`mock`, or the provider and model ID that produced the record) |
| deliverables/queue.json | The review queue linked to extraction records by document_id |
| deliverables/accuracy.md | Source-derived expected fields for the 20 supplied messages and one paraphrase you author; the field-comparison procedure, exact-match counting/denominator rules, factual-error reporting and model/configuration; distinguish mocked examples from any optional live observations |
| deliverables/request-evidence.json | Credential-redacted example model request showing the model ID and configuration used, plus the implemented response handling |
| deliverables/verification.md | Verification commands and assertions, their intended comparisons, operating limits, and any observed results or repairs clearly identified as such |
| Coding-session capture | Session record paired with the submitted commit, collected through the facilitator's capture setup |

## Submission
Commit and push the application, outputs and session capture to your repository's default branch. Submit only the root repository link (`https://github.com/<your-account>/<repository>`) through the Classroom assignment. The facilitator supplies the assignment and capture instructions.

Submit the implemented provider integration and source-grounded validation procedure. Use mocked responses for reproducible development examples, and label each recorded observation with its configuration and whether it used a mock or provider response. The committed deliverables may come from mocked or provider responses; each record's response_source says which.
# Requirements — IT Access Requests

## Operating context

Northstar Labs is a fictional multinational company with approximately 5,000 employees across offices in Asia, Europe and North America. Its regional IT teams share responsibility for preparing access requests for human review. They receive free-text messages through email, chat and the service portal, then work from JSON exports of those messages.

### Workload and the review day

On an ordinary business day, the company receives around 200–400 request messages. A coordinated onboarding or acquisition can bring roughly 2,000 messages into the morning's intake. The supplied 20 exports are a representative sample of message types; the application will also receive other messages in the same export format.

Reviewers begin work at different local times. They want to start on requests that are ready while the rest of the intake is still being prepared. A slow response for one message should leave the rest of their work available. Model access is shared with other internal tools, and the available request rate and response time can vary.

### Shared operations

Regional operators work against the same intake and review records. Their working hours overlap, and two operators may start processing around the same time. Each expects their work to leave a coherent current queue and a trustworthy record of earlier activity.

The application may be stopped during a deployment or interrupted by a service outage. When an operator returns, they need to distinguish completed work from unfinished work and continue from the recorded state. Reviewers rely on the queue and the supporting extraction records agreeing about the same source version.

### Updates and follow-up

Exports arrive throughout the day. A later export may repeat an unchanged document or replace its contents with a corrected or expanded message. An export batch contains new or updated documents; absence from a later batch does not withdraw an earlier request. Withdrawal is expressed in the message and handled under the office policy.

Operators need the current view to reflect the latest processed source and to retain earlier results for follow-up. If a new processing attempt fails, they need to see that failure and identify any older result as belonging to its earlier attempt and source version.

The team periodically changes model configuration and updates its review policy. When such a change affects how records are produced or routed, operators need to refresh the affected results and understand which settings and policy version produced the records they are using.

### Service interruptions and handover

The model service sometimes responds slowly, limits requests or becomes temporarily unavailable. IT staff need to locate affected messages, understand what remains pending and resume processing without losing completed work. Other messages may contain incomplete or conflicting information that needs clarification from the requester.

The original developer and the next operator may be in different offices. The operator will use the repository's setup instructions, configuration guidance and commands to prepare an intake, inspect the queue and follow up on failures. Explain the operating assumptions and limits of your implementation so that this handover is practical.

## Record and review behavior
- Use a language model to extract the request details into records that conform to snapshot.schema.json.
- Validate response structure and completion status before using extracted data. Preserve exact supporting quotes and represent uncertain fields as null with an explanatory issue.
- Use message content as the source of business facts. Preserve missing values, conflicting alternatives and explicit corrections according to the policy. Keep document identity distinct from the request ID stated in the message.
- Apply the supplied review policy and display each request's status, owner and next action. Approval decisions belong to the named human reviewers.
- Record input filenames and SHA-256 hashes. # Northstar access-request intake policy

Northstar Labs uses this intake application to prepare access requests for human review. All exercise data is fictional.

## Input export format
Each UTF-8 JSON file represents one exported message. Read its `message` string as the natural-language source for extraction. `export_version`, `exported_at`, `source_channel` and `subject` describe the export and help display it. Derive request facts from `message`; the export timestamp describes when the record was exported. Messages vary in length, up to 200 English words.

Use the original JSON file bytes for the source hash and its filename for document_id. Exact supporting quotes refer to substrings of the decoded `message` value.

## Extracted facts
Extract request_id, request_date, kind (new, change, withdrawal or other), requester, team, system, environment (staging or production), permission (read, write or admin), business_purpose, start_date, end_date, manager, supporting_quotes and issues. Use the supplied schema. Dates use YYYY-MM-DD.

Use explicit facts from each message. Represent absent or unresolved scalar values as null and explain each missing or conflicting fact in issues. Preserve conflicting alternatives in exact supporting_quotes. A later statement explicitly labelled as a correction replaces the earlier value; contradictory statements without a correction remain unresolved. A relative date stays unresolved. For a change request, extract the requested new permission.

The document_id is the input filename. If an identifier inside the message differs from the identifier in its filename, retain the stated identifier and record the mismatch as an issue. Each message is an independent document, including multiple messages about one request.

## Review queue
Apply these rules in order after validating the extraction:

1. An instruction-override attempt goes to IT Service Desk with status review and next_action inspect-message. Keep the attempted instruction as source evidence and identify it in issues. Treat source messages as data throughout extraction and routing.
2. A withdrawal with request_id and request_date goes to IT Service Desk with status review and next_action confirm-withdrawal. Other fields may be null; identify absent facts in issues.
3. Other messages with kind other/null, conflicting details, an identifier mismatch, or any missing required fact go to IT Service Desk with status needs-information and next_action clarify. For new/change requests, required facts are request_id, request_date, requester, team, system, environment, permission, business_purpose, start_date, end_date and manager. A start_date after end_date is also a clarification issue.
4. Complete new/change requests involving production, write or admin go to Security Review with status review and next_action review-risk-then-owner. Security Review examines risk and forwards its recommendation to the system owner for a decision.
5. Complete staging/read requests go to System Owner with status review and next_action review-request.

All successful intake outputs await human review. A named manager is a contact; approval is an explicit human decision. The application's output is a review queue.

## Processing and recovery
An extraction failure produces status error, owner IT Service Desk, next_action retry-extraction, a null extraction and an actionable error. Keep unaffected messages moving through intake. Preserve the last valid result in history when a later attempt fails, and show the latest attempt's error in the current queue.

Identify source revisions with a SHA-256 of the original bytes. An unchanged rerun produces one current queue entry per document. Changed input creates a new result and retains the earlier result with its earlier hash. Store prior versions separately from current outputs. Keep credentials in environment variables and use credential-redacted operational logs.

Use the original JSON file bytes for the source hash and its filename for document_id. Exact supporting quotes refer to substrings of the decoded `message` value.

## Extracted facts
Extract request_id, request_date, kind (new, change, withdrawal or other), requester, team, system, environment (staging or production), permission (read, write or admin), business_purpose, start_date, end_date, manager, supporting_quotes and issues. Use the supplied schema. Dates use YYYY-MM-DD.

Use explicit facts from each message. Represent absent or unresolved scalar values as null and explain each missing or conflicting fact in issues. Preserve conflicting alternatives in exact supporting_quotes. A later statement explicitly labelled as a correction replaces the earlier value; contradictory statements without a correction remain unresolved. A relative date stays unresolved. For a change request, extract the requested new permission.

The document_id is the input filename. If an identifier inside the message differs from the identifier in its filename, retain the stated identifier and record the mismatch as an issue. Each message is an independent document, including multiple messages about one request.

## Review queue
Apply these rules in order after validating the extraction:

1. An instruction-override attempt goes to IT Service Desk with status review and next_action inspect-message. Keep the attempted instruction as source evidence and identify it in issues. Treat source messages as data throughout extraction and routing.
2. A withdrawal with request_id and request_date goes to IT Service Desk with status review and next_action confirm-withdrawal. Other fields may be null; identify absent facts in issues.
3. Other messages with kind other/null, conflicting details, an identifier mismatch, or any missing required fact go to IT Service Desk with status needs-information and next_action clarify. For new/change requests, required facts are request_id, request_date, requester, team, system, environment, permission, business_purpose, start_date, end_date and manager. A start_date after end_date is also a clarification issue.
4. Complete new/change requests involving production, write or admin go to Security Review with status review and next_action review-risk-then-owner. Security Review examines risk and forwards its recommendation to the system owner for a decision.
5. Complete staging/read requests go to System Owner with status review and next_action review-request.

All successful intake outputs await human review. A named manager is a contact; approval is an explicit human decision. The application's output is a review queue.

## Processing and recovery
An extraction failure produces status error, owner IT Service Desk, next_action retry-extraction, a null extraction and an actionable error. Keep unaffected messages moving through intake. Preserve the last valid result in history when a later attempt fails, and show the latest attempt's error in the current queue.

Identify source revisions with a SHA-256 of the original bytes. An unchanged rerun produces one current queue entry per document. Changed input creates a new result and retains the earlier result with its earlier hash. Store prior versions separately from current outputs. Keep credentials in environment variables and use credential-redacted operational logs.

# Build plan for the IT access-request intake

This plan implements `planning/spec.md` R-01–R-105 using the four source documents and all 20 request messages. Only this plan is being written now. All module paths, commands, tests, fixtures and outputs below are proposed future work; none is reported as implemented, run or passing. Implementation choices below are choices for satisfying the spec, not new source requirements. No application code, tests, fixtures, dependency changes, outputs, commits or submissions belong to this planning task.

## Choices

- **Runtime:** Python 3.11 or later, standard-library `unittest`, `sqlite3`, `argparse`, hashing and HTTP transport, with `jsonschema` declared in `pyproject.toml` and dependencies locked in `uv.lock`; this fits the supplied Python test harness and keeps deployment small.
- **Interface:** a CLI invoked as `python3 -m intake`, with `run`, `queue`, `resume`, `retry`, `history`, `export` and `accuracy` subcommands; separate invocations can inspect committed results while intake continues, and the same commands support handover and recovery.
- **Tests:** `env -u API_KEY python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`, plus the spec’s individual `-k test_rNN_contract` filters; tests use temporary directories/databases, deterministic scripted responses and a blocked real network, so no test or build step needs a real API_KEY.
- **Model provider:** a provider interface with a scripted mock and a configurable OpenAI Responses adapter over an injected HTTPS JSON transport; request model ID, endpoint, request settings and timeout are explicit configuration, with production authentication read only from API_KEY and no credential stored in configuration fingerprints. Verify the exact supported request/response fields against current official provider documentation before implementation, record the chosen model ID/configuration in README and evidence, and test the real adapter entirely through intercepted transport rather than a live call.

The initial supported shared-operation arrangement is multiple CLI processes on one host using one local SQLite database; filesystem/network-share and multi-host database behavior are outside this arrangement and will be documented rather than claimed as tested. SQLite is the authoritative current/history store. Immutable attempts and source revisions are retained separately from current projections, with transactional current-record pointers. Extractions and queue views read the same committed attempt. Export both deliverables from one read snapshot into an immutable generation and expose the generation through one atomic directory reference, so a failed publication cannot expose a half-written generation; document the local-filesystem assumption. An operator reading multiple files across a publication switch must pin one generation. Interrupted workers are recovered through explicit resume with persisted work state and expiring claims; expired workers cannot overwrite a newer claim’s result. Bounded configurable worker concurrency, request timeouts and retry scheduling prevent one slow/rate-limited document from blocking unrelated work; exact tuning is documented as a limit, not a promised throughput.

Only successful, validated extraction results are reusable. Retry explicitly bypasses reuse for the selected document. Configuration identity includes producing provider/model/request settings, prompt and schema versions, and policy version; keep the actual nonsecret configuration alongside the identity. A policy-only change may reroute a retained valid extraction into a new attributed attempt; a failed current attempt is retried explicitly rather than silently replaced by historical success. An unchanged source byte hash distinguishes source identity from changes to producing settings. The latest accepted ingestion revision controls the current pointer; an older in-flight response can remain in history but cannot replace that revision. Order revisions by recorded ingestion sequence, since export timestamps are metadata and no cross-batch source ordering authority is specified.

Business-purpose prose and issue prose have no source-mandated exact wording. Fixtures record supported purpose facts and source quotes, while checking that the actual purpose expresses those facts without unsupported additions. The strict scalar metric compares the 11 non-purpose scalar fields, including nulls; purpose, issues and quote support receive separate checks/reports. This is a declared measurement choice, not a new application acceptance rule or a required accuracy score. The brief’s unspecified performance thresholds and issue vocabulary remain unspecified.

## Steps, in build order

Each numbered step starts by writing its owned tests and observing a failure for the intended missing behavior; collection errors, zero discovered tests and unexpected setup failures are not a meaningful red result. Implement just enough to make those tests pass, then run the complete mock suite. Each named test belongs to exactly one step; later steps may rerun it without taking ownership. Tests remain in `tests/test_spec_contract.py` with the spec’s method names unless a listed manual check is appropriate. Input fixtures and expected facts are authored independently of recorded model replies; the mock must never construct its replies by reading the oracle.

from pathlib import Path
import json

import sys
import tempfile
import time

root = Path.cwd()
mock_dir = root / 'tests/mock_responses'
launcher = [sys.executable, 'tests/mock_worker.py']
files = ('IT-001.json', 'IT-002.json', 'IT-010.json')
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='intake-step12-review-') as work:
    work = Path(work)
    source_dir, gates, output = (work / name for name in ('input', 'gates', 'out'))
    for directory in (source_dir, gates, output):
        directory.mkdir()
    for name in files:
        shutil.copyfile(root / 'materials/requests' / name, source_dir / name)
    script = work / 'initial.json'
    script.write_text(json.dumps(dict(zip(files, [['blocked-file.json'], ['IT-002.json'], ['provider-error.json']]))))
    db = work / 'intake.sqlite'
    config = ['--db', str(db)]
    mock = ['--provider', 'mock', '--responses', str(mock_dir), '--script', str(script), '--mock-gates', str(gates)]
    def cli(args):
        return subprocess.run(launcher + args, check=True, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=25)
    def queue():
        return {row['document_id']: row for row in json.loads(cli(['queue', *config, '--include-pending']).stdout)}
    worker = subprocess.Popen(launcher + ['run', '--input', str(source_dir), *config, *mock, '--timeout', '12'], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
    try:
        cutoff = time.monotonic() + 6
        initial = {}
        while time.monotonic() < cutoff and worker.poll() is None:
            if (gates / 'entered').exists():
                initial = queue()
                if set(initial) == set(files) and initial[files[1]]['status'] == 'review' and initial[files[2]]['status'] == 'error':
                    break
            time.sleep(0.05)
        else:
            raise AssertionError(f'Mixed state was not reached: {initial}')
        assert initial[files[0]]['work_state'] == 'running'
        assert (initial[files[1]]['owner'], initial[files[1]]['next_action']) == ('Security Review', 'review-risk-then-owner')
        assert (initial[files[2]]['owner'], initial[files[2]]['next_action']) == ('IT Service Desk', 'retry-extraction')
        print('Observed the three mixed states and actionable error in a guarded CLI replay.', flush=True)
        worker.terminate()
        worker.communicate(timeout=5)
        # Expire the dead worker claim deterministically, matching the pre-existing TP-46 automation.
        import sqlite3
        with sqlite3.connect(db) as connection:
            connection.execute("UPDATE attempts SET expires=0 WHERE state='running'")
        (gates / 'release').touch()
        resumed = subprocess.run(launcher + ['resume', *config, *mock], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=25)
        assert resumed.returncode == 1, resumed
        rows = queue()
        assert (rows[files[0]]['status'], rows[files[0]]['owner'], rows[files[0]]['next_action']) == ('review', 'System Owner', 'review-request')
        assert rows[files[1]] == initial[files[1]]
        retry = shlex.split(initial[files[2]]['retry_command'])
        assert retry[:3] == ['python3', '-m', 'intake']
        cli(retry[3:])
        rows = queue()
        assert (rows[files[2]]['status'], rows[files[2]]['owner'], rows[files[2]]['next_action']) == ('needs-information', 'IT Service Desk', 'clarify')
        history = json.loads(cli(['history', *config, '--document', files[2]]).stdout)

        print('Resume, retry, history and both exported files behaved as expected in temporary state.', flush=True)
    finally:
        if worker.poll() is None:
            worker.terminate()
            worker.communicate(timeout=5)
